entries.content_plain:
CHAPTER 7
1Sa 7:1 , 2 . The Ark at Kirjath-jearim.
1. the men of Kirjath-jearim-- "the city of woods," also Kirjath-baal ( Jos 15:60 ; 18:14 ; 1Ch 13:5 , 6 ). It was the nearest town to Beth-shemesh and stood on a hill. This was the reason of the message ( 1Sa 6:21 ), and why this was chosen for the convenience of people turning their faces to the ark ( 1Ki 8:29-35 ; Psa 28:2 ; Da 6:10 ).
brought it into the house of Abinadab in the hill-- Why it was not transported at once to Shiloh where the tabernacle and sacred vessels were remaining, is difficult to conjecture.
sanctified ... his son-- He was not a Levite, and was therefore only set apart or appointed to be keeper of the place.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2555"/><div sID="gen3458" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2555"/><hi type="bold">2. the ark abode in Kirjath-jearim ... twenty years--</hi>It appears, in the subsequent history, that a much longer period elapsed before its final removal from Kirjath-jearim (<reference osisRef="2Sam.6.1-2Sam.6.19">2Sa 6:1-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.13.1-1Chr.13.14">1Ch 13:1-14</reference>). But that length of time had passed when the Israelites began to revive from their sad state of religious decline. The capture of the ark had produced a general indifference either as to its loss or its recovery.<div eID="gen3458" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3459" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">all the house of Israel lamented after the Lord--</hi>They were then brought, doubtless by the influence of Samuel's exhortations, to renounce idolatry, and to return to the national worship of the true God.<div eID="gen3459" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3460" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1Sam.7.3-1Sam.7.6">1Sa 7:3-6</reference>. The Israelites, through Samuel's Influence, Solemnly Repent at Mizpeh. <div eID="gen3460" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
2. the ark abode in Kirjath-jearim ... twenty years-- It appears, in the subsequent history, that a much longer period elapsed before its final removal from Kirjath-jearim ( 2Sa 6:1-19 ; 1Ch 13:1-14 ). But that length of time had passed when the Israelites began to revive from their sad state of religious decline. The capture of the ark had produced a general indifference either as to its loss or its recovery.
all the house of Israel lamented after the Lord-- They were then brought, doubtless by the influence of Samuel's exhortations, to renounce idolatry, and to return to the national worship of the true God.
1Sa 7:3-6 . The Israelites, through Samuel's Influence, Solemnly Repent at Mizpeh.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2556"/><div sID="gen3461" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2556"/><hi type="bold">3-6. Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel--</hi>A great national reformation was effected through the influence of Samuel. Disgusted with their foreign servitude, and panting for the restoration of liberty and independence, they were open to salutary impressions; and convinced of their errors, they renounced idolatry. The re-establishment of the faith of their fathers was inaugurated at a great public meeting, held at Mizpeh in Judah, and hallowed by the observance of impressive religious solemnities. The drawing water, and pouring it out before the Lord, seems to have been a symbolical act by which, in the people's name, Samuel testified their sense of national corruption, their need of that moral purification of which water is the emblem, and their sincere desire to pour out their hearts in repentance before God. <div eID="gen3461" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2558"/><div sID="gen3464" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2558"/><hi type="bold">7-11. when the Philistines heard, &c.--</hi>The character and importance of the national convention at Mizpeh were fully appreciated by the Philistines. They discerned in it the rising spirit of religious patriotism among the Israelites that was prepared to throw off the yoke of their domination. Anxious to crush it at the first, they made a sudden incursion while the Israelites were in the midst of their solemn celebration. Unprepared for resistance, they besought Samuel to supplicate the divine interposition to save them from their enemies. The prophet's prayers and sacrifice were answered by such a tremendous storm of thunder and lightning that the assailants, panic-struck, were disordered and fled. The Israelites, recognizing the hand of God, rushed courageously on the foe they had so much dreaded and committed such immense havoc, that the Philistines did not for long recover from this disastrous blow. This brilliant victory secured peace and independence to Israel for twenty years, as well as the restitution of the usurped territory. <div eID="gen3464" type="x-p"/>
